sentences.zh: 我在凌晨四点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.zh: 在太空的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，这是《访谈》。

sentences.en: I'm David Marchese.
sentences.zh: 我是大卫·马尔凯塞。

sentences.en: If I ask you to think of a Richard Linklater movie, what do you think of?
sentences.zh: 如果我让你想起一部理查德·林克莱特（Richard Linklater）的电影，你会想到什么？

sentences.en: Maybe it's the cult favorite Days of Confused.
sentences.zh: 也许是邪典最爱《年少轻狂》。

sentences.en: That's the movie that launched Matthew McConaughey's career.
sentences.zh: 那是开启马修·麦康纳（Matthew McConaughey）演艺生涯的电影。

sentences.en: Or maybe it's Before Sunrise, the first installment of his beloved trilogy about big ideas, love, and fate.
sentences.zh: 或者也许是《爱在黎明破晓前》，他备受喜爱的三部曲的第一部，讲述宏大观点、爱与宿命。

sentences.en: Or maybe you'd think about the low-key, coming-of-age epic Boyhood, which Linklater famously filmed over a dozen years.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会想到低调的成长史诗《少年时代》，林克莱特历时十多年拍摄，这广为人知。

sentences.en: And of course, you can't forget School of Rock, his biggest hit, which exists in a category all of its own.
sentences.zh: 当然，你不能忘记《摇滚校园》，他最卖座的电影，它自成一格。

sentences.en: And to me, that's the fun of Linklater's work.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这就是林克莱特作品的乐趣所在。

sentences.en: You never quite know what he's going to make next.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道他接下来会拍什么。

sentences.en: So I wasn't surprised to see him getting into romantic crime thrillers with his new movie,
sentences.zh: 所以，看到他的新电影开始涉及浪漫犯罪惊悚片，我并不感到意外，

sentences.en: Hitman.
sentences.zh: 《杀手：代号？》。

sentences.en: It stars the great Glenn Powell, who also co-wrote it.
sentences.zh: 主演是伟大的格伦·鲍威尔（Glenn Powell），他也参与了编剧。

sentences.en: It's excellent.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But I would argue that it's excellent because it's actually not so far off from his other work as it might seem.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它出色是因为它其实并没有表面上看起来离他的其他作品那么远。

sentences.en: Between all the thrills, the crimes, and the sex, Hitman sneaks in a pretty provocative exploration of one of Linklater's favorite themes, the changing nature of identity.
sentences.zh: 在所有的惊悚、犯罪和性爱之间，《杀手：代号？》悄悄探讨了一个相当具有挑衅性的主题，这也是林克莱特最喜欢的主题之一：身份的不断变化。

sentences.en: Basically, what it means to be a person.
sentences.zh: 基本上，就是作为一个人的意义。

sentences.en: It's also a movie, as so many of Linklater's films are, that understands just how much fun it is to watch smart characters talk to each other, exploring ideas, making each other
sentences.zh: 正如林克莱特的许多电影一样，这也是一部明白观察聪明的角色互相交谈、探讨想法、互相逗

sentences.en: laugh, and even testing each other a little bit.
sentences.zh: 笑甚至稍微考验对方是多么有趣的事情的电影。

sentences.en: It's the talking that made me fall in love with Linklater's films, because those are the kinds of conversations that are most meaningful to me.
sentences.zh: 正是这种对话让我爱上了林克莱特的电影，因为那是对我而言最有意义的谈话方式。

sentences.en: I don't want to make too much of all this, but I can see a pretty clear line from teenage me sitting around watching Waking Life and Slacker over and over again, to me here now,
sentences.zh: 我不想把这一切过度解读，但我能看到一条相当清晰的轨迹：从十几岁的我坐在那里一遍又一遍地看《半梦半醒的人生》和《都市浪人》，到现在的我，

sentences.en: talking with those films' director, Richard Linklater, who, as it turns out, sounds a lot like a character from one of his movies.
sentences.zh: 与这些电影的导演理查德·林克莱特对话，结果发现，他听起来非常像他电影里的一个角色。

sentences.en: Here's our conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的对话。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say that a lot of your films are asking questions about identity and formation of identity.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以说，你的许多电影都在探讨关于身份以及身份形成的问题。

sentences.en: And given that that's a recurring theme in your work, I'm curious how you think about your identity at 63 years old, do you feel like it's fixed?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这是你作品中反复出现的主题，我很想知道你是如何看待你63岁时的身份的，你觉得它是固定的吗？

sentences.en: Do you feel like you still have formative experiences?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你仍然会有塑造人生观的经历吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Isn't that the question of self?
sentences.zh: 这不就是关于自我的问题吗？

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing I thought a lot about my entire life, you know, just like, what could transform me?
sentences.zh: 这是我一生都在思考的那种事情，你知道的，比如说，什么能改变我？

sentences.en: What could make me feel different than how I feel, how I see the world?
sentences.zh: 什么能让我感觉与现在的自己、看待世界的方式有所不同？

sentences.en: So I've always kind of monitored that, you know, like, what's going to change me?
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在某种程度上监控这一点，你知道的，比如，什么会改变我？

sentences.en: And I was probably more in the camp of, we're fixed, give or take, whatever, little percentage around the edges.
sentences.zh: 我可能更倾向于这种观点：我们的本质是固定的，大同小异，边缘有些许百分比的浮动。

sentences.en: And we sort of accept ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们算是在某种程度上接受了自己。

sentences.en: So I was more interested in this notion lately that, oh, you really can change, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以最近我对这种观点更感兴趣：哦，你真的可以改变，你知道吗？

sentences.en: You know, you really, the personality isn't fixed.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你真的可以，人格并不是固定不变的。

sentences.en: But that seems sort of current, you know, in a way, this notion of self and identity, you know, gender, anything.
sentences.zh: 但这在某种程度上似乎很时兴，你知道的，关于自我和身份的这种观念，性别，任何事情。

sentences.en: I sort of like that it's all on the table, that everybody's thinking like, well, you kind of are who you say you are, you know?
sentences.zh: 我有点喜欢一切都可以拿出来讨论，每个人都在想：嗯，你觉得自己是谁，你就是谁，你知道吗？

sentences.en: To me, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这很有趣。

sentences.en: Do you have a lot of different identities?
sentences.zh: 你有许多不同的身份吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, probably as many as anybody else.
sentences.zh: 对，可能和其他人一样多。

sentences.en: What are the different ones?
sentences.zh: 具体有哪些不同的身份？

sentences.en: Well, you know, if you get me on a ping pong table, like an area where, like, my third rail is athletics, you know?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，如果你把我弄到乒乓球桌上，比如这样一个领域——我的死穴是竞技体育，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I cross into this realm where I was acculturated and just good enough to, like, figure I should be good and achieve.
sentences.zh: 我进入了这个领域，我曾在那里接受过文化熏陶，而且技术刚好够好，让我觉得我应该表现出色并取得成就。

sentences.en: And I have this bar for myself.
sentences.zh: 我对自己的要求很高。

sentences.en: So I feel this little rush of competitiveness, which I really don't have in the world of art.
sentences.zh: 所以我感到了一丝竞争心带来的冲动，这种冲动我在艺术领域里真的没有。

sentences.en: At all.
sentences.zh: 一点也没有。

sentences.en: Or my life, even.
sentences.zh: 甚至在我的生活中也没有。

sentences.en: I don't see it anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我在任何地方都看不到它。

sentences.en: But it's in certain areas.
sentences.zh: 但它存在于某些特定领域。

sentences.en: And I try to avoid them because it's not the best me.
sentences.zh: 我尽量避开它们，因为那不是最好的我。

sentences.en: But every now and then, it can be fun to kind of push yourself.
sentences.zh: 但偶尔，逼自己一把也挺有意思的。

sentences.en: But, you know, I'm the guy looking at the world through glass.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道的，我是那个透过玻璃看世界的人。

sentences.en: You know, I was always the guy in the corner thinking about everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我总是那个在角落里思考一切的人。

sentences.en: I'm not an extrovert.
sentences.zh: 我不是外向的人。

sentences.en: I'm an introvert who gets put in extroverted situations occasionally.
sentences.zh: 我是一个偶尔被置于外向场合的内向者。

sentences.en: And I could play that role.
sentences.zh: 我能扮演好那个角色。

sentences.en: But roles I currently play, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但我目前扮演的角色，我不知道。

sentences.en: It's nice to care less about it as you get older.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄的增长，不再那么在乎这些其实挺好的。

sentences.en: About what?
sentences.zh: 在乎什么？

sentences.en: Like, consistency, maybe.
sentences.zh: 比如，连贯性吧。

sentences.en: Ah.
sentences.zh: 啊。

sentences.en: But my pure self is on the set making a movie.
sentences.zh: 但我最纯粹的自我是在片场拍电影的时候。

sentences.en: I'm pretty convinced.
sentences.zh: 我相当确信这一点。

sentences.en: The self that I've worked for and the pinnacle of my time and effort, I realize, is, you know, rehearsing and shooting the movie and whatever writing before.
sentences.zh: 我为之努力的自我，以及我时间和精力的巅峰，我意识到，你知道的，就是排练和拍摄电影，以及之前的任何写作。

sentences.en: Like, that's the pure me, but it's manufactured me, you know, catch me at dinner later and you get the same guy who's processing the shit of the day and, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如，那是最纯粹的我，但也是人造的我，你知道的，晚些时候在晚宴上抓住我，你就会看到同一个家伙，他正在消化当天的狗屁倒灶，然后，你知道的，

sentences.en: having his lectures about what I know and whatever lunatic political ideas that are flowing through my system in real time like everybody else.
sentences.zh: 发表他的长篇大论，谈论我所知道的事情，以及任何像其他人一样实时流淌在我系统中的疯狂政治想法。

sentences.en: But I process the world through art and, in particular, cinema.
sentences.zh: 但我通过艺术，特别是电影来消化世界。

sentences.en: And that's the space that I've been lucky enough to live in.
sentences.zh: 那是我有幸生活的空间。

sentences.en: What's a lunatic political idea that's in your system right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在脑子里有什么疯狂的政治想法吗？

sentences.en: Ah, you're really going to – well, you notice.
sentences.zh: 啊，你真的打算——好吧，你注意到了。

sentences.en: I don't really – if you're unfortunate enough to be sitting next to me at dinner or around me, I often just spout off.
sentences.zh: 我真的不——如果你不幸坐在我晚餐旁边或者我周围，我经常就会滔滔不绝。

sentences.en: But I don't have a need to share that publicly so much because I know it's not a long-term thought.
sentences.zh: 但我没有那么强烈的愿望去公开分享这些，因为我知道这不是长远之计。

sentences.en: But I guess the meticulous long-term nature of making a film is a certain kind of personality and someone who has to be on Twitter or whatever spouting off their moment-to-moment taking in and spitting out of the world.
sentences.zh: 但我想拍电影那种细致入微的长期性需要某种特定的人格，而那些必须泡在推特上或其他地方滔滔不绝地发表他们对世界瞬时吸收和吐纳的人则不同。

sentences.en: I have those ideas, but I know they have no value.
sentences.zh: 我有那些想法，但我知道它们毫无价值。

sentences.en: I know I'm not going to enlighten anyone, but I really do draw a line.
sentences.zh: 我知道我不会启迪任何人，但我确实划清了界限。

sentences.en: I'm like, yeah, I could mouth off like I could share my brain snot with the whole world the way everybody else did.
sentences.zh: 我想：是的，我可以像其他人一样大嘴巴，可以把我的脑浆分享给全世界。

sentences.en: But I don't see any value in it for me personally, you know, because I've been privileged, gifted, whatever you want to say, to make the greatest,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这对我个人没有任何价值，你知道的，因为我有幸、有天赋——随你怎么说——去创作有史以来最伟大、

sentences.en: most expressive storytelling art form ever invented.
sentences.zh: 最具表现力的叙事艺术形式。

sentences.en: So I'm one of the few who get to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我成了少数能够做到这一点的人之一。

sentences.en: So why would I put any effort into these transitory, weird little reactive areas?
sentences.zh: 那我为什么要把任何精力投入到这些短暂、奇怪、微小的反应性领域呢？

sentences.en: I think you should file away brain snot as a possible fictional band name in a film, the name of a punk EP, maybe a seven-inch brain snot.
sentences.zh: 我认为你应该把“脑浆”这个词存起来，作为电影中虚构乐队的名字、朋克EP的名字，也许是一张七英寸唱片的歌名。

sentences.en: That's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 那挺不错的。

sentences.en: Well, that's what so much of the world feels like, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，世界很大一部分不就是这种感觉吗，不是吗？

sentences.en: Brain snot?
sentences.zh: 脑浆？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, overactive, like conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 对，过度活跃，就像阴谋论一样。

sentences.en: You know, it's like it's activated brains, but just unfiltered, unaccredited.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就像是被激活的大脑，但完全未经筛选，未经证实。

sentences.en: What was kind of fun a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 很久以前觉得有点好玩的那种东西。

sentences.en: Oh, let's just say conspiracy or alternative thinking and all that just to see it metastasize into something so lethal and harmful.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们姑且称之为阴谋论或另类思维之类的好玩的东西，眼睁睁看着它恶化成如此致命和有害的东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, so it's kind of like, wow, I don't want to participate in that at all.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就好比，哇，我一点也不想参与其中。

sentences.en: You know, I want to ask you a question that connects a little bit more to Glenn Powell and Hitman where, you know, in the film,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我想问你一个与格伦·鲍威尔和《杀手：代号？》联系更紧密的问题，你知道的，在电影中，

sentences.en: Glenn Powell plays a half dozen or so different hitmen.
sentences.zh: 格伦·鲍威尔饰演了大概半打左右不同的杀手。

sentences.en: And he's assuming his character is assuming these different roles within the film.
sentences.zh: 他在电影中扮演的角色在扮演这些不同的角色。

sentences.en: And it's really sort of, I think, I hate to use a corny term, but it's kind of like a star making performance, you know?
sentences.zh: 这真的是一种，我想，我讨厌用一个老土的词，但这就有点像是一部造星演出，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And I think he's someone who people have a sense that, you know, this guy's a big star in the making.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们有一种感觉，觉得这家伙未来一定会成为巨星。

sentences.en: And you've done movies with a bunch of big stars.
sentences.zh: 你和一帮大明星合作过电影。

sentences.en: You know, you did, obviously, Matthew McConaughey's in The Newton Boys and Dazed and Confused and in Bernie.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，马修·麦康纳显然演过《年少轻狂》、《牛顿男孩》和《伯尼》。

sentences.en: You know, Keanu Reeves in A Scanner Darkly.
sentences.zh: 基努·里维斯演过《黑暗扫描仪》，你知道的。

sentences.en: Ben Affleck is, I mean, the list goes on.
sentences.zh: 本·阿弗莱克，我的意思是，名单还在继续。

sentences.en: Shirley MacLaine, Jack Black, both in Bernie.
sentences.zh: 雪莉·麦克雷恩、杰克·布莱克，两人都出演了《伯尼》。

sentences.en: And I always wondered, do you feel like, as a director, you understand what makes someone a star?
sentences.zh: 我一直很好奇，作为一名导演，你觉得自己能看出是什么造就了明星吗？

sentences.en: Every actor I work with, like, oh, this is a star to me.
sentences.zh: 我合作过的每一个演员，我都觉得：哦，对我来说这就是个明星。

sentences.en: I love him.
sentences.zh: 我爱他。

sentences.en: I think my camera loves him.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的镜头爱他。

sentences.en: I love the character.
sentences.zh: 我爱这个角色。

sentences.en: So it's always been a mystery to me what happens with people's, you know, futures.
sentences.zh: 所以人们的未来会怎样，对我来说一直是个谜。

sentences.en: You just don't know.
sentences.zh: 你根本无从知晓。

sentences.en: I think there's luck.
sentences.zh: 我认为有运气的成分。

sentences.en: There's a lot of elements involved that no one person's in control of, you know?
sentences.zh: 其中涉及很多因素，没有人能完全掌控，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Um, I don't think anyone's ever surprised me.
sentences.zh: 呃，我不认为有什么让我感到意外的。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not surprised when Matthew becomes a star or Ben Affleck or, you know, you look back and it all makes sense.
sentences.zh: 比如，当马修成为明星，或者本·阿弗莱克成为明星时，我并不感到意外，你知道的，回过头来看，这一切都说得通。

sentences.en: It's like, yeah, of course, they were great.
sentences.zh: 就像是，是的，理所当然，他们很棒。

sentences.en: They had this thing.
sentences.zh: 他们有那种特质。

sentences.en: You know, I'm probably more surprised others didn't get that opportunity or aren't seen as that or Hollywood doesn't know what to do with.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我可能更惊讶于其他人没有得到那样的机会，或者没有被那样看待，或者好莱坞不知道该拿他们怎么办。

sentences.en: But there's kind of an eternal mystery of opportunities and cultural moments that you get.
sentences.zh: 但机遇和所处的文化时刻存在着一种永恒的谜团。

sentences.en: And, you know, so I think Glenn's having one of those right now, perhaps, you know, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我认为格伦现在正经历其中之一，也许吧，你看上去是这样的。

sentences.en: But I think anyone who knows Glenn, who's worked with him in the last 10 years, would say, oh, that could have come 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但我认为任何了解格伦、在过去10年里与他合作过的人都会说：哦，这本该在10年前就发生了。

sentences.en: You know, Glenn is Glenn.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，格伦就是格伦。

sentences.en: He's got that star quality.
sentences.zh: 他有那种明星气质。

sentences.en: I've known that for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我很久以前就知道了。

sentences.en: Do you think actors can see in themselves the qualities that you as the director can see?
sentences.zh: 你认为演员能在自己身上看到你作为导演所能看到的那些特质吗？

sentences.en: And I'm thinking of an example that, you know, a few years ago, I interviewed Brad Pitt around the time of Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 我想起一个例子，几年前，在《好莱坞往事》上映期间，我采访了布拉德·皮特。

sentences.en: And I was asking him about this one specific scene where, you know, he just sort of like turns towards the camera a little and he's got this smile on his face.
sentences.zh: 我问他关于一个特定场景，你知道的，他只是稍微朝镜头转了一下身，脸上带着那种微笑。

sentences.en: It's just a perfect example of how star quality can make a scene.
sentences.zh: 这简直是明星气质如何成就一个场景的完美例子。

sentences.en: Like, and I was asking about it and it was clear he had no idea, like he didn't really remember the scene, had no idea what I was talking about.
sentences.zh: 比如，我问起这件事时，很显然他完全不知道，他真的不记得那个场景了，也不知道我在说什么。

sentences.en: And then, of course, after the interview was over, I realized like, oh, that was actually a question for Quentin Tarantino.
sentences.zh: 当然，采访结束后，我意识到，哦，其实那是给昆汀·塔伦蒂诺（Quentin Tarantino）提的问题。

sentences.en: Like, he understood something in that actor in that moment.
sentences.zh: 就像是他理解了那个演员在那个时刻的某种东西。

sentences.en: It's not about whether the actor knows him.
sentences.zh: 这与演员是否了解自己无关。

sentences.en: But do you think you see things in these personalities that they aren't aware of or don't?
sentences.zh: 但你认为你在这些个性中看到了他们自己没有意识到或不知道的东西吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's not the kind of thing you talk about consciously.
sentences.zh: 对，这不是那种你会刻意去谈论的事情。

sentences.en: There's nothing to be gained for telling the actor, well, you're such a star in this.
sentences.zh: 告诉演员“哦，你在里边太有明星相了”对你没有任何好处。

sentences.en: You don't need to, you know, you can just turn and look that.
sentences.zh: 你不需要，你知道的，你只要转过身去看那个就行了。

sentences.en: You know, you just say, hey, look over here and look that way.
sentences.zh: 你知道你在和什么打交道。

sentences.en: You know what you're dealing with.
sentences.zh: 你知道他们是明星。

sentences.en: You know they're a star.
sentences.zh: 而电影正是建立在那种明星魅力之上的。

sentences.en: And cinema rides on this kind of star charisma.
sentences.zh: 而电影正是建立在那种明星魅力之上的。

sentences.en: Brad Pitt knows he's a fucking star.
sentences.zh: 布拉德·皮特深知自己是个彻头彻尾的巨星。

sentences.en: That's been drilled into his head every day for the last 30 years.
sentences.zh: 过去三十年里，这个念头天天被灌输进他的脑海。

sentences.en: But maybe how it's used and, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 但或许这如何被运用，你知道的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: You know, I read, I think it was the New Yorker profile of you, probably around the time of boyhood.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我读过，我想那是《纽约客》对你的专访，大概是在《少年时代》上映那会儿。

sentences.en: And in there, it said that there was some point in your life as a young man where you were watching something like 600 movies a year.
sentences.zh: 里面提到，你年轻时的某个阶段，曾达到了每年看大约600部电影的程度。

sentences.en: You would go to a theater and watch three or four movies in a row.
sentences.zh: 你会去电影院一口气看三四部电影。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of us can relate to that feeling, especially in sort of early adulthood or late adolescence, of really like falling in love with an art form.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都能感同身受那种感觉，尤其是在初入成年或青春期晚期的时候，那种真正坠入爱河般迷恋一种艺术形式的感觉。

sentences.en: You almost get kind of drunk on it.
sentences.zh: 你简直会为之沉醉。

sentences.en: And I'm curious what the feeling you get from movies now is and how it's different from what it used to be.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，你现在从电影中获得的感觉是什么，它和过去有什么不同？

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't think you can ever replace that initial just passion and fury when you've discovered your art form and you just take it in with your entire being.
sentences.zh: 对，我想你永远无法取代那种最初的激情与狂热，当你发现你的艺术形式时，你用整个生命去全盘接受它。

sentences.en: And like, you know, I'd write down every movie I saw, 650 films a year.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我会记下我看过的每一部电影，一年650部。

sentences.en: I mean, that was really nothing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那其实不算什么。

sentences.en: And a lot of it, you know, looking back, it's like, oh, that's what you had to do.
sentences.zh: 而且回过头来看，很多时候你会觉得，哦，那是你当时必须要经历的。

sentences.en: You kind of you're transitioning from the real world to your world and your world.
sentences.zh: 你有点像是在从现实世界过渡到你的世界，还有你的世界。

sentences.en: In my case, it was it was just cinema, the arts or or this other world you want to live in, not the world you live in.
sentences.zh: 对我的情况而言，那就是电影、艺术，或者说是你想居住的另一个世界，而不是你实际生活的那个世界。

sentences.en: But it's different now.
sentences.zh: 但现在不一样了。

sentences.en: You know, I don't I don't have the need to see that many movies.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不再有那种看那么多电影的需求了。

sentences.en: I still love movies and still life dedicated to it.
sentences.zh: 我依然热爱电影，一生都将致力于此。

sentences.en: But, you know, you feed yourself in different ways.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你开始以不同的方式滋养自己。

sentences.en: Do you still get like the electricity or the jolt from seeing a film that you used to like?
sentences.zh: 你现在看电影时，还能像以前那样感受到那种触电般的震撼吗？

sentences.en: What's a recent movie that kind of blew the top of your head off?
sentences.zh: 最近有什么电影让你有那种脑洞大开的感觉吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 对，这是个好问题。

sentences.en: You know, no, I can't get the same jolt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不能了，我找不到那种相同的震撼了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I just you can't.
sentences.zh: 对，我就是……你找不到。

sentences.en: You can't get the same jolt.
sentences.zh: 你找不到那种相同的震撼了。

sentences.en: I can get a jolt, but it's a different kind of jolt.
sentences.zh: 我能获得震撼，但那是另一种震撼。

sentences.en: I know too much.
sentences.zh: 我知道得太多了。

sentences.en: I'm I'm behind the camera.
sentences.zh: 我……我身处摄像机背后。

sentences.en: I know what they're doing, but I can still, you know, I judge films on like, oh, what got my cinematic blood circulating?
sentences.zh: 我知道他们在做什么，但我依然可以，你知道的，我评价电影的标准是，哦，什么调动了我的电影血液？

sentences.en: What really kind of got me like, oh, that was cinema, you know, so maybe I kind of put zone of interest in that category.
sentences.zh: 是什么真正让我觉得，哦，这才是电影，所以也许我可以把《利益区域》归入那一类。

sentences.en: I was looking at that going, oh, you know, boom.
sentences.zh: 我当时看着它想，哦，你知道的，轰动。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a movie.
sentences.zh: 对，那才叫电影。

sentences.en: I think there's a sense currently that we're sort of in a weird moment for cinema.
sentences.zh: 我觉得目前有一种共识，即我们正处于电影的一个奇怪时期。

sentences.en: And I've even read interviews with you where you've wondered about whether the current generation of audiences value cinema and whether you came up during kind of like the last,
sentences.zh: 我甚至读过对你的采访，你在其中质疑过当今的观众是否还重视电影，以及你是否是在，可以说，最后……

sentences.en: I think the way you put it was the last good era of filmmaking.
sentences.zh: 我想你是这么说的：最后一个优秀的电影创作时代。

sentences.en: What makes you wonder those things?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你产生这些疑问的？

sentences.en: Like, why are those questions in your mind?
sentences.zh: 比如说，为什么你的脑海里会有这些问题？

sentences.en: Well, I don't think I said good era of filmmaking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不认为我当时说过“优秀的电影创作时代”。

sentences.en: I would say maybe the culture was different.
sentences.zh: 我会说也许当时的文化有所不同。

sentences.en: And it's always the last question.
sentences.zh: 而且这永远是最后一个问题。

sentences.en: You know, you're talking about your new movie.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你明明在谈论你的新电影。

sentences.en: It's always, well, what do you think about the state of cinema today?
sentences.zh: 结果总会变成，好吧，你觉得今天电影的现状如何？

sentences.en: And it's like, oh, be careful.
sentences.zh: 这就好像，哦，得小心了。

sentences.en: Because it's, I don't know, we're all prone to these overarching, big, important statements about the state of things.
sentences.zh: 因为，我不知道，我们都很容易对现状发表这种宏大、重要、概括性的言论。

sentences.en: And if you know anything about the history of cinema, that's all it's ever been.
sentences.zh: 如果你对电影史有所了解，就会知道电影一直以来都是这样的。

sentences.en: It's always been the end of cinema.
sentences.zh: 总有人说电影要完了。

sentences.en: Something was wiping it out.
sentences.zh: 总有什么东西在消灭它。

sentences.en: You know, even sound, color, technicolor, you know, cinemascope, TV, it's always been under threat.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，甚至连有声电影、彩色电影、宽银幕电影、电视，它一直都受到威胁。

sentences.en: It's always been very volatile feeling.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉一直非常动荡。

sentences.en: The industry's always threatened.
sentences.zh: 这个行业总是受到威胁。

sentences.en: I think because it's an industry that's prone to technological change.
sentences.zh: 我想这是因为它是一个容易发生技术变革的行业。

sentences.en: You know, things can come along and just wipe it out or change it pretty significantly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，随时会有新东西出现并彻底消灭它，或者带来相当显著的改变。

sentences.en: So it's different than painting or literature or other art forMs.
sentences.zh: 所以它不同于绘画、文学或其他艺术形式。

sentences.en: It's sort of technology and commerce are really nearby, kind of codependent within the art form.
sentences.zh: 技术和商业与艺术形式紧密相连，并且在其中互为依存。

sentences.en: So I think everyone's always on alert and everyone's always a little paranoid that the system that they've known is coming to an end.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为每个人总是保持警惕，每个人都总是有点偏执，担心他们所熟知的体制即将走到尽头。

sentences.en: Well, you're working currently on an adaptation of the Sondheim musical, Merrily We Roll Along, which the musical takes place over the course of 20 or so years.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你目前正在改编桑德海姆的音乐剧《Merrily We Roll Along》，这部音乐剧跨越了大约20年的时间。

sentences.en: And your plan, sort of like what you did with Boyhood, where you filmed it over a period of years and years,
sentences.zh: 你的计划，有点像你拍《少年时代》那样，历时数年进行拍摄，

sentences.en: is that you're filming your adaptation of Merrily We Roll Along over 20 years or so.
sentences.zh: 就是你要把这部《Merrily We Roll Along》的改编版拍摄大约20年左右。

sentences.en: At least that's the plan.
sentences.zh: 至少计划是这样的。

sentences.en: And so when you finish this movie, I guess with the caveat, if you finish this movie.
sentences.zh: 所以当你拍完这部电影时，我想还得加上一个前提，如果你能拍完这部电影的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Throw that in there, please.
sentences.zh: 请把这个也算进去。

sentences.en: You're going to be over 80 years old.
sentences.zh: 你将年过八旬。

sentences.en: I'll be about 80.
sentences.zh: 我大概80岁吧。

sentences.en: And so it's going to be kind of a life and career capstone, I would think.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这大概会成为你人生和职业生涯的巅峰之作。

sentences.en: So tell me why that project, given how, like the place you know it's going to occupy in your life and your career.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我，考虑到这个项目在你的生活和职业生涯中将占据的位置，为什么偏偏是它？

sentences.en: You want to hear something that's technically insane, and I admit it?
sentences.zh: 你想听一件技术上极其疯狂、而我也承认的事吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: You said capstone to a career at age 80.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说80岁是职业生涯的巅峰之作。

sentences.en: I've never thought that.
sentences.zh: 我从来没这么想过。

sentences.en: Ah.
sentences.zh: 啊。

sentences.en: Because I see myself making a film when I'm like 94.
sentences.zh: 因为我看到自己94岁的时候还在拍电影。

sentences.en: I really do.
sentences.zh: 我真的是这么想的。

sentences.en: So I don't, I think it's like, oh yeah, you know, those years will go along.
sentences.zh: 所以我不觉得，我觉得这就好像，哦对，你知道的，那些年头会过去的。

sentences.en: I'll try to stay in shape, try to be healthy, hope to get lucky.
sentences.zh: 我会努力保持身材，努力保持健康，希望能走运。

sentences.en: And, you know, I just, I mean, I'm not an idiot.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我只是……我的意思是，我不是个傻子。

sentences.en: I know, you know, but it's all at the behest of, we're telling a story that takes place over 20 years, and it's really important for this story to work,
sentences.zh: 我知道，你知道的，但这完全是为了服务于这样一个故事：我们讲述一个跨越20年的故事，为了让这个故事成立，至关重要的一点是，

sentences.en: that you feel those years go by.
sentences.zh: 你要能感受到岁月的流逝。

sentences.en: So it's the same reason that, you know, boyhood put its, you know, that was boyhood.
sentences.zh: 所以原因是一样的，你知道的，《少年时代》也把它的……那就是《少年时代》。

sentences.en: You had to feel life going by.
sentences.zh: 你必须感受到生活在流逝。

sentences.en: And this movie's about long-term, you know, friendship and the way life treats people and how that shifts around over 20 years.
sentences.zh: 这部电影讲的是长期的友谊，你知道的，生活如何对待人们，以及这种关系在20年里如何发生转变。

sentences.en: But, you know, I just think you can, in the arts, you can will things into existence.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我只是觉得在艺术领域，你可以用意志力让某些事情成为现实。

sentences.en: And if people are passionate about it, you make it happen.
sentences.zh: 如果人们对它充满热情，你就能把它变成现实。

sentences.en: You know, everybody involved in that is clearly doing it because they care.
sentences.zh: 你知道，参与其中的每个人显然都是因为他们在乎才去做的。

sentences.en: So we just have to assume they'll keep caring and they'll care 10 years, 15, 16, 17 more years.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只需假设他们会继续在乎，并且在未来10年、15、16、17年里一直都在乎。

sentences.en: But, you know, you judge people on that.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你是凭这一点来评判人们的。

sentences.en: You go, oh, before I cast them, I go, you're a lifer, you know, you're going to be doing this.
sentences.zh: 你会想，哦，在我选角之前，我会想，你是个愿意奉献一生的人，你知道的，你会一直做下去。

sentences.en: I did that on boyhood.
sentences.zh: 我拍《少年时代》时就是这么做的。

sentences.en: I asked Patricia Arquette, like, what are you going to be doing 12 years from now?
sentences.zh: 我问帕特里夏·阿奎特：你12年后会在做什么？

sentences.en: And she's like, I'm going to be probably looking for a part to play.
sentences.zh: 她说：我大概还在找角色演吧。

sentences.en: I said, yeah, and I'm going to be trying to make a film.
sentences.zh: 我说：好极了，那我会在努力拍电影。

sentences.en: So let's just start now and we'll be who we are now and in the future.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在就开始吧，我们现在是什么样，将来就是什么样。

sentences.en: And that's all it was.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: It's not some huge leap of faith.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么巨大的信仰飞跃。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's blowing my mind that you could say this movie that I'm going to spend 20 years making that I'm going to finish when I'm 83.
sentences.zh: 你竟然能说出这部我要花20年时间去拍、直到83岁才能拍完的电影……

sentences.en: I'll be 80.
sentences.zh: 我会是80岁。

sentences.en: Hey, don't add any more.
sentences.zh: 嘿，别再给我加岁数了。

sentences.en: I mean, they're going to be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们将会是……

sentences.en: But that's solely because that's sort of what you think the film itself is demanding and not because it's like a meaningful, overarching statement of some sort.
sentences.zh: 但这纯粹是因为你觉得电影本身在要求这样做，而不是因为这是一种有意义的、某种宏大的表态？

sentences.en: If anybody spent 20 years working on something, you'd say, well, that says something about who they are and what's important to them.
sentences.zh: 如果有人花20年时间做一件事，你会说，这说明了他们是谁，说明了什么对他们最重要。

sentences.en: Telling a well-told story the right way is what means the most to me.
sentences.zh: 用正确的方式讲好一个故事，才是我最看重的。

sentences.en: You know, finding the form that meets the content.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，寻找与内容相匹配的形式。

sentences.en: That's what a director does.
sentences.zh: 这正是一个导演该做的事。

sentences.en: You feel not just the story, but how to tell it, what it should look and feel like.
sentences.zh: 你不仅能感受到故事本身，还能感受到如何去讲，它应该看起来是什么样、感觉是什么样。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I like long.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢漫长的过程。

sentences.en: So many art forms are fairly quick.
sentences.zh: 很多艺术形式都相当快餐。

sentences.en: I think cinema has the ability to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为电影有能力做到……

sentences.en: You know, I love that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: It's at the Whitney, that Jay DeFeo painting, the rose.
sentences.zh: 在惠特尼美术馆里，杰·德费奥的那幅画，叫《玫瑰》。

sentences.en: Have you ever seen it?
sentences.zh: 你见过吗？

sentences.en: It's huge, right?
sentences.zh: 它很大，对吧？

sentences.en: It's huge.
sentences.zh: 它非常大。

sentences.en: It's thick.
sentences.zh: 它很厚。

sentences.en: It's like a foot thick because she spent so many years painting layers of paint on it.
sentences.zh: 它有一英尺厚，因为她花了整整好几年时间在上面一层又一层地画颜料。

sentences.en: I just love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: I find it so moving, just knowing the effort.
sentences.zh: 光是知道这份付出，我就觉得太感人了。

sentences.en: First, it's a stunning work, but how did it get so thick and just, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 首先，这是一件惊艳的作品，但它是怎么变得这么厚的，还有，你知道，总之。

sentences.en: I mean, most artists, we have found the right therapy for our conditions or whatever neurological conditions we're dealing with.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大多数艺术家，我们都已经为我们的心理状况或任何我们正在应对的神经系统状况找到了合适的疗法。

sentences.en: But, you know, everyone's just wired a little different.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，每个人的思维方式都有点不同。

sentences.en: So I admit that about myself and just go with it.
sentences.zh: 所以我承认我身上有这一点，然后顺其自然。

sentences.en: It's like, okay, well, it's the way my brain works.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，好吧，这就是我的大脑运作的方式。

sentences.en: Do you have some sort of contingency plan?

sentences.zh: 不是以一种消极的方式。

sentences.en: Just, you know, I just see life as kind of fleeting.
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道的，我只是觉得生命有点转瞬即逝。

sentences.en: Is that bad?
sentences.zh: 这样不好吗？

sentences.zh: 这听起来像是你某部电影里的人物会提出的问题。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，一想到我不会永远留在这里，就觉得有种诗意。

sentences.en: No one is.
sentences.zh: 没有人会永远留下。

sentences.zh: 但我对此并不病态。

sentences.en: I just kind of acknowledge life passing and all of us being here for a little while.
sentences.zh: 我只是有点意识到生命的流逝，以及我们所有人都在这里停留一小会儿。

sentences.en: And it's kind of beautiful that we're all here crossing paths at the same moment.
sentences.zh: 而且我们所有人都在同一时刻在这里交汇，这感觉有点美妙。

sentences.en: I liked astronomy and I liked science and just knowing how old everything was and how brief humans are in lifespans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢天文学，喜欢科学，也知道万物存在了多久，以及人类的寿命是多么短暂。

sentences.en: I'm like, oh, we really are insignificant.

sentences.en: So that scares some people, but I love that feeling.
sentences.zh: 这让有些人感到害怕，但我很喜欢这种感觉。

sentences.zh: 我喜欢这种在宇宙中是如此随机和渺小的感觉。

sentences.en: I'm maybe going to put this question in slightly pretentious terms, but I think given that I'm

sentences.en: talking to Richard Linklater and certainly there are conversations in your films that some
sentences.zh: 和理查德·林克莱特交谈，而且你的电影中确实有些对话

sentences.en: other people might say are slightly pretentious, I'm going to give myself permission to do it.
sentences.zh: 别人可能会说有点自命不凡，那我也允许自己这么做一次。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm fine with that.
sentences.zh: 行，我没问题。

sentences.en: But I was just reading about this poet, Delmore Schwartz, and he has this poem called
sentences.zh: 但我刚刚读到关于这位诗人德尔莫·施瓦茨的文章，他有一首诗叫

sentences.en: Sarah's, like the painter George Sarah's Sunday Afternoon.
sentences.zh: 《萨拉》，就像画家乔治·萨拉的《大碗岛的星期天下午》。

sentences.en: And it's all about the artist as someone who observes life, but doesn't fully participate in it.
sentences.zh: 这首诗讲的就是艺术家作为一个观察生活的人，却没有完全参与其中。

sentences.en: So I read that and I was then thinking about you and your films, because I think of your films as really having all these sort of very closely and intimately observed moments of
sentences.zh: 所以我读了之后，就想到了你和你的电影，因为我认为你的电影里真的有所有这些非常紧密且亲密观察到的时刻

sentences.en: what on the surface just seemed like normal life.
sentences.zh: 表面上看，这些时刻似乎只是普通的生活。

sentences.en: You know, it could be two people walking and talking, you know, or just throughout boyhood, there's countless scenes of just normal life.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，可能是两个人边走边聊，或者在整部《少年时代》里，有无数日常生活的场景。

sentences.en: That's all it is.
sentences.zh: 这就是全部内容了。

sentences.en: And then I thought, well, what is your interest in that have to do with or how does it affect your sense of observation of your real life when it's happening?
sentences.zh: 然后我想，嗯，你对此的兴趣与此有何关系，或者当真实生活发生时，它如何影响你对真实生活的观察感？

sentences.en: Like, are you always sort of sitting back and observing life kind of from a distance?
sentences.zh: 比如，你是不是总是有点像坐在后方，从远处观察生活？

sentences.en: Always.
sentences.zh: 一直都是。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the curse.
sentences.zh: 对，这就是诅咒。

sentences.en: I'm in the moment.
sentences.zh: 我身处当下。

sentences.en: I'm out of the moment.
sentences.zh: 我又抽离于当下。

sentences.en: It kind of robs you of the in-the-moment experience.
sentences.zh: 这有点剥夺了你身处当下的体验。

sentences.en: But then there's also kind of a mentality, I think, not uncommon to writers and film people is like, this will only be real when I process it through my art form.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我想作家和电影人身上也有一种不太罕见的心态，那就是：“只有当我通过艺术形式加工它时，这才是真实的。”

sentences.en: Like, something terrible is happening right in front of you.
sentences.zh: 就像，可怕的事情正发生在你的眼前。

sentences.en: You know, your loved one's dying or relationship's ending.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你爱的人正在死去，或者一段关系正在结束。

sentences.en: And you're like, oh, you're just processing it, not in the moment, but like, I'm going to have a character in a movie someday experience this, and I'm going to try to capture this,
sentences.zh: 你会想，哦，你只是在加工它，不是在当下体验，而是像：我总有一天要在电影里让一个角色经历这个，我要试着捕捉这个，

sentences.en: what I just felt very, very deeply.
sentences.zh: 我刚才感受得非常非常深的这种情感。

sentences.en: But you're robbing yourself and the person you're with or whatever of that moment.
sentences.zh: 但你却剥夺了你自己、和你在一起的人或者其他人的那个当下。

sentences.en: But maybe it's a self-preservation way of just taking something and storing it away or processing it through.
sentences.zh: 但也许这是一种自我保护的方式，只是把某些东西拿走并储藏起来，或者通过这种方式来加工它。

sentences.en: So I share that, you know, like, oh, nothing's really real until I make it work in a movie in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以我也有同感，你知道的，比如，“哦，直到我以某种方式把它做进电影里，一切才真正变得真实。”

sentences.en: Maybe we'll get into it when we talk again.
sentences.zh: 也许我们下次再聊时会深入探讨这个。

sentences.en: But I really have questions about the last 15 minutes of Hitman.
sentences.zh: 但我对《杀手信徒》最后15分钟确实有一些疑问。

sentences.en: And one of the ideas of the film is that sort of we, and this is something we talked about earlier, is that we all have the power to create our own identity.

sentences.en: And the film then suggests that that includes the identity of someone capable of murder and then living seemingly happily after having committed murder.
sentences.zh: 然后电影暗示，这其中也包括拥有一个有能力谋杀、并且在谋杀后似乎能幸福生活的身份。

sentences.zh: 如果你还没看过，你想告诉大家那部纪录片是关于什么的吗？

sentences.zh: 它确实探讨了死刑，主要是从那些参与其中的杀戮机器、即国家批准的谋杀部分的人的角度切入。

sentences.en: But, you know, the questions posed by your documentary about how people basically find
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，你的纪录片提出的问题——关于人们基本上是如何找到

sentences.en: and the state-sanctioned killing of other people, also reminded me of how you mentioned

sentences.en: people go about their lives right beside something awful happening.
sentences.zh: 可怕的事情就在身边发生的同时继续他们的生活。

sentences.zh: 我想知道，你觉得自己是否理解人们是如何能够做到那种心理隔离的？

sentences.en: Like, did you learn anything about people from making your documentary?
sentences.zh: 比如，你通过制作纪录片了解到了关于人们的什么事情吗？

sentences.en: I've always been fascinated by that, you know, how we can compartmentalize.
sentences.zh: 我一直对这一点很着迷，你知道的，我们是如何做到心理隔离的。

sentences.en: You know, and if you spread around the horror of abomination, you know, just think of the way we treat animals.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你把这种暴行和邪恶扩散开来，你知道的，想想我们对待动物的方式。

sentences.en: If you eat meat, you are supporting a really super cruel, horrible system that creates incredible pain and suffering.
sentences.zh: 如果你吃肉，你就是在支持一个非常残酷、可怕的系统，它制造了难以置信的痛苦和折磨。

sentences.en: And you've been a vegetarian for a long time, right?
sentences.zh: 你吃素很久了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you can't make it through the modern world without, you know, pushing out the horror show that is a lot of life, right?

sentences.en: But, you know, we're all doing this little psychic dance to let ourselves think we're not horrible people.

sentences.en: And, you know, I have this whole, you know, we're suing the state of Texas right now.

sentences.zh: 我的朋友，伯尼·蒂塔，我们刚刚……

sentences.en: Oh, the real life inspiration for your movie, Bernie.
sentences.zh: 哦，你电影《伯尼》中真实生活中的灵感来源。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's the lead plaintiff in a seat.
sentences.zh: 对，他是诉讼中的首席原告。

sentences.en: We're going to hopefully change...
sentences.zh: 我们希望改变……

sentences.en: They have just an unbelievably cruel system where they don't have to air condition state prison cells.
sentences.zh: 他们的系统冷酷得令人难以置信，州立监狱的牢房甚至不需要配备空调。

sentences.en: They do federal, they do local jails, they do for animal facilities, but somehow you don't have to for state.
sentences.zh: 联邦监狱有，地方监狱有，动物收容所也有，但不知为什么州立的就不需要有。

sentences.en: And it's just horrible.
sentences.zh: 这简直太可怕了。

sentences.en: I mentioned it in my documentary, the heat conditions, not only for corrections officers, but for the inmates.
sentences.zh: 我在我的纪录片里提到过，这种酷热条件不仅对狱警如此，对囚犯也是如此。

sentences.en: So we've juSt...
sentences.zh: 所以我们刚刚……

sentences.en: There's this big lawsuit that we really think will change a lot of people's lives for the...
sentences.zh: 这是一场大型诉讼，我们真的认为它会为很多人的生活带来改变，为了……

sentences.en: So I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道。

sentences.en: You go into political realms and you can...
sentences.zh: 你涉足政治领域，你可以……

sentences.en: That's a whole nother.
sentences.zh: 那是完全不同的另一码事。

sentences.en: You could dedicate your entire life to trying to make the world a better place.
sentences.zh: 你可以将你的整个一生奉献于试图让世界变得更美好。

sentences.en: But I pick my spots, you know.
sentences.zh: 但我有选择地关注，你知道的。

sentences.en: You know, can I bring up something?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我能提个醒吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: It was only after the thing for the next hours I processed and just all the thoughts I did not articulate very well.
sentences.zh: 就在那之后的一小时里，我一直在加工所有那些我没有表达得很清楚的想法。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 说吧。

sentences.en: Which is everything.
sentences.zh: 也就是所有的想法。

sentences.en: Most of what I say.
sentences.zh: 我大部分说过的话。

sentences.en: When you were asking if I felt...
sentences.zh: 当时你问我是否觉得自己……

sentences.en: And it was a poignant, important question, I think.
sentences.zh: 这是一个尖锐且重要的问题，我认为。

sentences.en: I just don't think I raised to the question.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得我没有达到那个问题的高度。

sentences.en: It was, what's your relation now to the work back then?
sentences.zh: 那是，你现在和当年作品的关系是什么？

sentences.en: Are you as passionate?
sentences.zh: 你还像以前一样充满激情吗？

sentences.en: Are you still seeing 600 moves a year?
sentences.zh: 你还在一年看600部电影吗？

sentences.en: How different?
sentences.zh: 有多大不同？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I really had to think about that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我真的不得不思考这个问题。

sentences.en: And my analysis of that is, you're a different person with different needs.
sentences.zh: 我对它的分析是，你是一个有着不同需求的不同人了。

sentences.en: And a lot of that is based on just confidence.
sentences.zh: 这里面很大一部分其实都建立在自信之上。

sentences.en: When you're starting out in an art form or anything in life, you can't have confidence because you don't have experience.
sentences.zh: 当你刚开始接触一种艺术形式或生活中的任何事物时，你不可能有自信，因为你没有经验。

sentences.en: But you have to be pretty confident to, say, make a film.
sentences.zh: 但你要说去拍一部电影，那就得相当自信。

sentences.en: So the only way you counterbalance that lack of experience and confidence is just absolute passion, full-on dedication, kind of fanatical spirit.
sentences.zh: 所以，要弥补经验和自信的不足，唯一的办法就是绝对的热情、全身心的投入，以及一种狂热的精神。

sentences.en: And I've had this conversation over the years with, you know, filmmaker friends.
sentences.zh: 这些年来，我跟一些电影人朋友也聊过这个话题。

sentences.en: Am I as passionate as I was in my 20s?
sentences.zh: 我还像二十多岁时那么充满热情吗？

sentences.en: Would I risk my whole life?
sentences.zh: 我会豁出整条命吗？

sentences.en: If it was my best friend or my negative drowning, which do I save?
sentences.zh: 如果落水的是我最好的一位朋友还是我的负片，我该救哪个？

sentences.en: The 20-something self goes, I'm saving my film.
sentences.zh: 二十来岁的自己会说，我要救我的电影。

sentences.en: Good luck, fucker.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运，混蛋。

sentences.en: And now it's not that answer.
sentences.zh: 现在可不是这个答案了。

sentences.en: And I'm not ashamed to say that, you know, because all that passion doesn't just go away.
sentences.zh: 而且我并不以此为耻，你知道的，因为所有的热情并没有凭空消失。

sentences.en: It disperses a little healthfully.
sentences.zh: 它以一种健康的方式稍微分散开来了。

sentences.en: I'm much more passionate in this world about a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 在这个世界上，我对很多事情都更有热情了。

sentences.en: You know, the most fascinating relation we all have is obviously to ourselves at different times in our lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们所有人经历过最奇妙的关系，显然是在人生不同阶段与自己的关系。

sentences.en: And you look back and it's like, God, I'm not as passionate as I was at, you know, 25.
sentences.zh: 当你回首过去，就会觉得，天哪，我怎么没有25岁时那么热情了。

sentences.en: It's like, thank God.
sentences.zh: 就会觉得，谢天谢地。

sentences.en: That was a crazy fuck, that person.
sentences.zh: 那家伙当年就是个疯子。

sentences.en: Very insecure.
sentences.zh: 非常没有安全感。

sentences.en: Very, you know, you're better than that now.
sentences.zh: 非常……你知道的，你现在比那时候强多了。

sentences.en: And you're, you're chiller, maybe a better person, less selfish.
sentences.zh: 你现在更淡定了，也许是个更好的人，没那么自私。

sentences.en: And it's, you look back at it as kind of heroic or something necessary.
sentences.zh: 你会把过去看作是一种英勇的行为，或者是某种必要的东西。

sentences.en: And it is, it absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It makes total sense.
sentences.zh: 完全说得通。

sentences.en: But I don't think you can do that forever.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你不可能永远那样生活。

sentences.en: If that's the only way you can work, you're not in it maybe for the long haul.
sentences.zh: 如果那是你唯一的工作方式，你或许就无法长久地干下去。

sentences.en: Well, you know, uh, probably 23 or however many years ago, I was just laying on the floor high out of my mind watching Waking Life thinking, how can I get inside that movie?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，大概在23年前还是多少年前，我只是躺在地板上，脑子嗨得不行，看着《半梦半醒的人生》，心想，我怎么才能进入那部电影里呢？

sentences.en: I'm much happier to be talking to you today than to be laying stoned on my floor watching
sentences.zh: 比起当年躺在自家地板上嗑大麻看

sentences.en: Waking Life.
sentences.zh: 《半梦半醒的人生》，我今天能和你聊天要高兴得多。

sentences.en: And I still love Waking Life.
sentences.zh: 我依然很喜欢《半梦半醒的人生》。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Um, thank you very much for taking the time to talk with me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常感谢你花时间和我交谈。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: I really have gotten a lot out of your movies over the years.
sentences.zh: 这些年来，我从你的电影里受益匪浅。

sentences.en: So thank you for that too.
sentences.zh: 所以也谢谢你这一点。

sentences.en: Really nice talking to you too.
sentences.zh: 和你聊天也非常开心。

sentences.en: We'll do it again, I'm sure, sometime.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，以后我们还会再聊的。

sentences.en: And have the first Merrily interview 17 years from now.
sentences.zh: 还要在17年后进行第一次《Merrily》的采访。

sentences.en: All right, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 好的，那就这么定。

sentences.en: Put in the calendar.
sentences.zh: 记到日历上。

sentences.en: It's on.
sentences.zh: 就这么说定了。

sentences.zh: 那是理查德·林克莱特。
